points.description: States the property as a single unique path between every pair of nodes, so the tree has no loops. Equivalent wording is accepted, such as a loop-free subnet that connects all nodes, which means no duplicate packets are forwarded.

Explains that multicast group membership is added to the link state packets, so every node learns the full topology and group membership. Each node then computes the multicast spanning tree locally, for example with Prim's or Kruskal's algorithm. Equivalent wording is accepted.

rubric.notes: Full mark (1) requires both the loop-free, unique-path property (P1) and the link-state modification where group membership is flooded in link state packets and each node builds the tree locally from the full topology (P2). Each point is all-or-nothing and worth half a mark. Naming a specific algorithm such as Prim or Kruskal is an example, not a requirement, so any correct local tree-construction method earns P2.
